$comment: #FEED-224: THE column fit of a Markdown table (a GFM pipe table in the Markdown leaf: every chat, comment, description and result), HAND-AUTHORED and replayed by src/table-fit.test.ts (`fitTableColumns`, the TS reference; the web renderers measure the DOM in web/table-fit.ts and call it), apps/desktop/crates/eui-core/tests/table_fit.rs (`fit_table_columns`; gpui paint/markdown.rs), the Swift (`MarkdownTableFit`) and Compose (`MarkdownTableFit`) tests. Before it every native painter split the box into EQUAL columns and the web left it to the browser's auto table layout at 100% width, where an unbreakable issue chip took the whole row and squeezed its neighbours to one letter per line. THE MEASURE (each renderer's own text engine): per column `min` = the widest piece its line breaker never splits (a word; a chip or an inline code span counts WHOLE, as an atom) and `max` = the widest cell laid out on one line, over the header (in its semibold) and the body cells, in CONTENT px (no padding). `available` = the Markdown's width less each column's two horizontal cell paddings and the table's own borders. THE FIT (inputs and outputs in whole px): `available` floors; each `min` ceils and is capped at `wordCap` (a longer word breaks, a wider chip truncates at its column) and each `max` ceils and is at least that min. The mins do not fit (Σmin ≥ available) = every column gets its min and the table SCROLLS sideways inside the box (it never squeezes a column under its min). Every column fits on one line (Σmax ≤ available) = every column gets its max and the table HUGS its content (start-aligned; it never stretches a short table across the box). Else WATER-FILL: one level L with Σ clamp(L, min, max) = available, so a column whose max is under L keeps its one line and the others share the rest evenly (never under their min); each width = clamp(floor(L), min, max) and the pixels left over go one each to the columns still growing at L (min ≤ the breakpoint under L < max), left to right. The table is Σwidths + the paddings + the borders wide. The genUI Table COMPONENT keeps its EXP-1548 columns (a fixed `width`, else an equal share never under `tableColumnMin`, cells truncate or wrap, a wider table scrolls): its columns are typed data, not prose.

cases.name: the FEED-224 shape: a short column, a long unbreakable chip column, a long prose column
everything fits on one line: the table hugs its content
the minimums overflow: each column its min, the table scrolls
a chip wider than the cap counts the cap
a capped chip column still grows past the cap when there is room
leftover pixels go left to right
a short column keeps its line while wide ones share the rest
a min above the level holds
one prose column fills the box
a max under its capped min lifts to it
eight columns on a phone scroll at their mins
